Tawaraya colour tests

Masanori Umeda’s drawing for Tawaraya, the boxing-ring bed shown at the first Memphis exhibition.

Source
M+, Hong Kong: Colour tests, Tawaraya (ring), bed (CA28/6/2)
Creator
Umeda Masanori
Made
May 1981
Style
Memphis (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Playful, theatrical, ironic
Evidence
Downloaded the museum’s published image (705 × 1000 px) from M+ to a private scratchpad and inspected it with the Read tool on 2026-09-25. No image is stored in the catalogue. The file holds seven items; only the first image was inspected. The finished bed itself was not seen.
Reviewed
25 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

M+ describes the file as drawings that test colour patterns for the design, some printed with the words “banchetto, dialogo, godimento, sapienza”. Ink on paper, May 1981, seven items. M+ record.

An M+ magazine article by curator Ikko Yokoyama (2021) says Tawaraya was shown at the first Memphis exhibition in Milan on 18 September 1981. It describes a boxing ring with black-and-white striped edges, a tatami centre, multicoloured ropes, and lamps on four posts, 280 × 280 × 120 cm. M+ Magazine.

The same article says Sottsass named it after a Kyoto ryokan, and that Fabio Cirifino photographed the Memphis designers sitting in it in 1981. M+ Magazine.

Observed

  • An isometric drawing shows a square ring on a base of heavy black-and-white vertical stripes.
  • Pink ropes run between four posts; each post ends in a small globe on a coiled stem.
  • Inside are pale tatami panels, cushions tinted in soft rainbow gradients, and a small red square tray.
  • Four large kanji and the Italian words banchetto, dialogo, godimento, and sapienza are placed at the corners.
  • Handwritten at the bottom: “Mobili ‘4 ½’ Maggio 81 Umeda”.

Why it belongs

The drawing combines Memphis’s black-and-white stripes with a sport object and a Japanese room type. It shows the group’s method of combining references from unrelated contexts.

Borrow

Use a heavy black-and-white striped band as a base or frame, with light pastel color inside.

Draw in isometric to present an object as a small stage or a toy.
